name: Dumbbell Multi-Planar Lunge
summary: A dynamic lower-body exercise that moves through sagittal, frontal, and transverse planes by lunging in multiple directions with dumbbells held at the sides.

setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, holding a light dumbbell in each hand at your sides with a neutral grip.
Brace your core, draw your shoulders slightly back, and fix your gaze straight ahead.
steps: Step forward into a front lunge, lowering until your back knee hovers just off the floor, then push forcefully back to the starting position.
Step directly out to the side into a lateral lunge, sitting your hips back over the working heel while keeping the trailing leg straight, then drive back to center.
Step backward at a diagonal angle into a reverse lunge, descend with control, and push back to the starting stance.
Continue cycling through the target directional sequence, then repeat the pattern on the opposite leg.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as you step out and lower into each lunge; exhale forcefully as you push through your foot to return to standing.

common_faults.fault: Allowing the lead knee to cave inward during lateral or diagonal lunges.
common_faults.correction: Actively press the knee outward so it tracks in line with your second and third toes.

common_faults.fault: Rounding the lower back or collapsing the torso forward when lunging.
common_faults.correction: Maintain an upright torso by bracing your abdominals and keeping your chest lifted.

precautions: Ensure a wide, clear perimeter of floor space in all directions before beginning.
Use light loads to prioritize balance and multi-planar joint control over heavy resistance.
